input.content: Anti-pattern: premature removal of a backward-compat read fallback during an in-progress data migration. A reader that handled both a legacy shape and a new shape (e.g. `if "destination" in row: return row["destination"]["address"]; return row["address"]`) was "cleaned up" to assume only the new nested shape. This raises KeyError on any un-migrated record. Safe only AFTER migration completes for all records. Signals to check: README/docs stating "read both shapes until migration finishes", mixed-shape data fixtures still present, background/batched migration with no startup gate. Tests masked the regression because they only covered the new write shape, never the legacy shape. Lesson: removing a compatibility branch is a deferred-removal item gated on migration completion + telemetry showing zero legacy records, not an immediate cleanup.
